relationship: Additive, explicitly versioned display extension. Frozen field-mapping.json describes the original baseline; these additional recipe values apply only when recorded in an image displayAdjustments and this document is manifest-hashed. Older baselines retain their recorded square-pixel and auto-min-max-v1 policy.

padding.pixelPaddingMin: Lower inclusive stored-sample endpoint from PixelPaddingValue (0028,0120) and optional PixelPaddingRangeLimit (0028,0121), interpreted with PixelRepresentation/BitsStored
padding.pixelPaddingMax: Upper inclusive stored-sample endpoint; a missing range limit selects just PixelPaddingValue
padding.rule: Exclude these samples before deriving automatic extrema; apply rescale afterward and order the transformed endpoints, including negative slopes. Window center=(low+high+1)/2 and width=max(1,high-low+1), recorded at Java float precision. Keep original source pixels unchanged. If every sample is padding and no complete source window is present, reject the preview explicitly. Source-supplied window pairs remain unchanged.

geometry.geometrySource: First supplied applicable pair: selected frame PixelMeasuresSequence.PixelSpacing, root PixelSpacing, ImagerPixelSpacing, NominalScannedPixelSpacing, then PixelAspectRatio
geometry.pixelAspectRatio: Normalized row-height:column-width, represented as rowRatio:1. Values retain row-before-column order. A non-square ratio changes PDF placement and interactive image geometry without altering pixels.
geometry.validation: The first present pair must contain two finite positive values; PixelAspectRatio requires positive integers. Zero spacing is permitted only for its singleton image dimension and supplies no usable ratio, so display defaults to 1:1. Pilot display ratios are bounded to 1e-6 through 1e6; unsupported geometry is reported, never silently replaced by a lower-priority supplied tag.
geometry.units: Unitless display ratio, not calibrated patient measurements, patient orientation or a GSDF display calibration

verification: Reparse original source values and re-render using the recorded policy. A recorded policy selects compatibility behavior; its numeric values are never trusted as source evidence. New recipes validate their source padding/geometry. Existing source-window-0, auto-min-max-v1 and square-pixel recipes remain reproducible.
